fixes.explanation: Festus is the governor who answered that since Paul had appealed to Caesar, to Caesar he would go (Acts 25:12). So he's part of how Paul ended up on this trip. But the text says the prisoners are handed over to a centurion named Julius (Acts 27:1). I think a governor has better things to do than ride along on a boat.

The winds. They sail to the lee of Cyprus "…because the winds were against us." (Acts 27:4). The lee is the side that blocks the wind, so the island helps shield them. It's like ducking around the corner of a building when the wind hits you right in the face.

Alexandria. Julius finds an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and puts them on board (Acts 27:6). That's the ship that finally goes where they're headed. It's like waiting forever at the stop and the right bus finally rolls up with Italy on the sign.

The pilot. The centurion "…was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship." (Acts 27:11). The text puts it just like that: contrary to Paul's advice, those two are the ones who persuaded him. Paul's advice is the one he went against.

The prisoners aren't named among the ones who persuade him. The text says the centurion "…was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship." (Acts 27:11). Paul himself is a prisoner, and he's the one who gave advice (Acts 27:10). The text says Julius was persuaded contrary to that advice.
The lifeboat was just hoisted up on board (Acts 27:17). The text doesn't have the crew tying the ship to it. What the crew does next is use ropes to undergird the ship. They pass the ropes under it.
That's the text. "…we abandoned all hope of being saved." (Acts 27:20). No sun, no stars, and the storm still battering them. I think this one hurts.

A bigger ship isn't in his words. Paul says, "…you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss." (Acts 27:21). His point is about his advice not to sail from Crete, friend.

The ship. Paul says there will be no loss of life, "…but only of the ship." (Acts 27:22). The cargo and tackle are already going over the side (Acts 27:18-19). The loss of life is the thing Paul says won't happen.

Yes. The angel says, "Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar." (Acts 27:24). The angel also says God has granted him the lives of all who sail with him. So Paul has somewhere to be, storm or no storm.
